name: The Universe
description: The universe from the Big Bang to today: the first galaxies, the Sun and its planets, and how telescopes, probes and great scientists found out how it all works.

checkpoints.name: The early universe
checkpoints.note: The universe begins in the Big Bang. Within a few hundred million years the first stars and galaxies shine, and the Milky Way forms. Generations of stars make the elements of which planets and people are made.

checkpoints.name: How the planets formed
checkpoints.note: A cloud of gas and dust collapses into the Sun and a disk of planets. Rock and ice clump into worlds, a collision makes the Moon, and the planets settle into their orbits.

checkpoints.name: Watching the sky
checkpoints.note: Babylonians, Greeks, Chinese, Indians and Maya chart the sky with the naked eye. Ptolemy puts the Earth at the centre, and Copernicus puts the Sun there instead.

checkpoints.name: The telescope age
checkpoints.note: Galileo turns a telescope on the sky. Kepler and Newton explain the orbits, new planets are found, Einstein rewrites gravity and Hubble shows that the universe is expanding.

checkpoints.name: Probes and great telescopes
checkpoints.note: Spacecraft visit every planet. Radio telescopes hear the echo of the Big Bang, the Hubble and Webb telescopes see the first galaxies, planets are found around other stars, and black holes are photographed.
